changelog: v5.1 — withdraw the correlation taper; keep the allocator retune. v5.0 violated product-decision D6 ('never trail SPY for long stretches', a first-class acceptance bar): RDD3y 0.057->0.094, worst-3y-excess -39.2->-53.1%, longest-underwater-vs-SPY 1591->2629 days, share of start cohorts still behind SPY at the end 20.4->26.4%. I promoted v5.0 without measuring D6 — the checklist had the stress gate, diff:holdings, both-halves and concentration, but not the trailing bar. A 14-config sweep isolates the cause: the ALLOCATOR retune (tau .008->.004, vol_suppressor_k 20->40) is innocent and free — CAGR 18.16->18.31%, Martin 3.642->3.703, RDD3y and longest-underwater unchanged. The TAPER is entirely responsible, monotonically: onset .80 -> RDD3y .094, .85 -> .063-.069, .90 -> no binding at all (Growth's max avgCorr is 0.89). There is no free region, because trimming correlated equity during a bull IS trailing SPY during a bull. v5.1 therefore keeps the free half and withdraws the costly half. The taper mechanism and its evidence stand (correlation predicts forward co-drawdown t=-4.51 with zero return effect t=0.01); the fix is to scale it by the trend regime so it cannot act in strong uptrends — next build. Net vs v4.3: CAGR +0.15pp, Martin +0.061, D6 intact.
